synopsis: OSI is the message standard used by sensor models delivered as FMUs, and it is among the open standards that make heterogeneous tool chains practical for road ADAS engineering [f13235, f9331]. Chapter 11 identifies Persival as offering credible sensor-model development and validation, including OSI FMUs and weather benches; its middle-cost example stack includes one externally validated sensor model, potentially an OSI FMU from a specialist [f8812, f9287]. However, ASAM’s 2025 high-fidelity OSI project states that existing abstractions insufficiently represent some physical phenomena, notably camera spectral irradiance and radar raw waveform data [f7081]. That project explicitly considers camera, radar and lidar, with ultrasound only a possibility, so the corpus pairs practical OSI-based integration options with unresolved fidelity limitations [f7082, f7081, f8812, f9287].
